category_title: Students who exhibit frustration-based crying and self-abusive behavior during long tasks
minimal_context: Shaun is sitting in the classroom and is presented with a stapled packet of reading worksheets to complete.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Shaun, here is your stapled packet of reading worksheets. Please start working on them.

STUDENT: (Looks at the stapled packet of worksheets and engages in off-task behavior, making a low grunting noise.)

TUTOR: You need to focus on your reading. Just do your best.

STUDENT: (Starts whining and making uninterpretable, garbled vocalizations instead of looking at the worksheets.)

TUTOR: Keep trying. Let me know if you have a question.

STUDENT: (Begins crying and engaging in self-abusive behavior, showing he is easily frustrated by the long packet of worksheets.)

options.A: Model appropriate reading behavior for the student, instructing them to complete the worksheets the same as the tutor.
options.B: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time completing the packet of reading worksheets.
options.C: Remain within 0.3 meters of the student when giving instructions or answering questions about the reading worksheets.
options.D: Prompt the student to call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll the class for help.
